title: I Printed the Group-Project Git History for the Slide Who Did Nothing

parts.text: I merged the repo at 1:14 a.m. before the demo. The classmate who owned "the slides" had zero commits and a deck full of our screenshots. I was twenty. I printed the git log, put it behind the last slide as an appendix, and let him present. The professor asked who wrote the appendix. I said git did. He got a different grade. I got sleep after. Screenshots are not authorship. Appendices are a love language. The repo still exists. So does the log. I would do group work alone before I would do it as a ghostwriter for a deck.

social.video_title: Zero commits, full screenshots, an appendix with teeth — Part 1/1
social.description: 1:14 a.m. merge, a slide owner, git as a witness. Would you have left the appendix out to keep peace?
